claims.statement: A reviewer confirms the shell hierarchy remains understandable across its responsive presentations.
The shell exposes a named main region and, at the viewport's width, a visible named navigation landmark.
Keyboard users can skip directly to the main region.
The shell fills the captured viewport while its content columns remain min-width safe.
Navigation and header chrome remain inside the viewport while main content scrolls.
Shell chrome labels remain single-line controls at every captured viewport, truncating rather than wrapping.

component.purpose: The one application frame a generated scenario mounts: brand, a SidebarShell-owned navigation column or icon rail, a BottomNav-owned phone tab bar or drawer, an optional header strip, a skip link, and a routed main pane that scrolls or fills. Navigation is data; the router plugs in through renderLink and onNavigate.
component.title: AppShell

elements.description: The named primary navigation landmark inside the column.
The named phone tab bar landmark.
The routed content region, scrolling or filling.

states.description: Sidebar density with a phone tab bar: the shape a generated scenario mounts.
Icon-over-label rail for a product whose primary surface needs the width.
Below the md breakpoint the column is a drawer behind a menu button; above it nothing changes.
The routed page owns the pane and pins its own header and composer.
An optional global strip above the routed content, present at every width.
Counts on navigation items in the column and the tab bar, labelled so they are never colour alone.
Long labels truncate inside the column instead of widening it; a disabled destination stays visible and inert.
Right-to-left layout with the column anchored to the inline start.
